text:
mira: Spot check found raw service-account JSON embedded in our partner webhook payloads stored in gs://partner-webhooks/2026-05-03/. Looks like a consumer wrote the full blob before the scrubber ran. Needs immediate triage.

owen: Can you paste a redacted snippet and the object path? Need to scope blast radius.

mira: path: gs://partner-webhooks/2026-05-03/payload-77.log 
snippet (redacted): `{"timestamp":"2026-05-03T07:12:11Z", "payload": "...\"client_email\":\"svc-ingest@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com\",\"private_key_id\":\"efgh-xxxx\"..."}`

satya: Treat as compromised until proven otherwise. Immediate: revoke keys, rotate SA, pause partner read access to that prefix. Keiko, can infra pause the bucket replication?

keiko: Paused replication and removed public read. Also added a temporary hold and ACL to restrict to sec/ops.

sec-bot: automated-alert: Vault audit shows several unwrap operations around 2026-05-03T07:10Z for secrets under secret/data/webhook/svcs. Ticket SEC-4230 created.

owen: If unwraps occurred, plaintext may have been emitted by our service before shipping. Satya: who owns the webhook consumer code?

satya: webhook-consumer team owns it. I'll page them and ask for a binary search of logs to see if they logged decrypted payloads.

linda: Quick containment checklist I propose: 1) Generate new key for svc-ingest SA and disable old key. 2) Reissue short-lived tokens for CI and services that used the SA. 3) Run a Vault/KMS policy audit to find any cross-project decrypt grants.

mira: Agreed. Also snapshot the raw object into a forensic bucket before making changes: gs://forensic-2812346789/obj-77.log (ACL: security-only). We need evidence for legal/partner.

keiko: Snapshot created and ACL set.

satya: I've opened rotate request: infra-runbook -> `./runbooks/rotate-sa-key.sh svc-ingest@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com` will create a new key, push to secret store, and revoke the old. Starting now.

sec-bot: automated-update: SEC-4230 -> containment in progress, forensic_snapshot: gs://forensic-2812346789/obj-77.log.

owen: RBAC question: how did partner write the blob? Did they have permission to PUT objects with content that includes secrets? We should check what agents had write access to that prefix and whether any cloud functions or ingestion jobs echo payloads.

linda: I'll run an IAM diff: `gcloud storage buckets get-iam-policy partner-webhooks` and inspect object-level ACLs. Also grep Cloud Functions logs for writes that include "private_key_id".

mira: Found a consumer lambda `webhook-forwarder-v1` that logs full request bodies to stderr on debug mode. That instance deployed in March. It likely wrote raw body to the object store for later replay.

satya: Disable debug logging in that function and redeploy a scrubbed version. Also add an ingest-time scrubber to redact fields: private_key, private_key_id, client_email.

keiko: Function debug logging disabled and a new commit pushed to disable PII body dumps. Redeploying now.

linda: Vault/KMS integration note: If wrapped ciphertexts were stored instead of plaintext, rotation strategy differs: we must remove partner decrypt grants and schedule a rewrap for all secrets that used that key. If plaintext was stored, rotate SA keys immediately.

nowen: sec-bot earlier flagged unwraps. Linda, can you map the KMS key used and any IAM bindings for external principals?

linda: Key in question: projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/webhooks/cryptoKeys/svc-keys. Current IAM policy includes `serviceAccount:partner-a@partner-123.iam.gserviceaccount.com` with decrypt role. That's unexpected. Opening SEC-4231 to remove that binding.

satya: Remove binding but coordinate with partner communications. Legal must sign off on request to purge any partner copies. We'll mirror forensics to them.

mira: Also, add CI test for the ingestion pipeline to assert bodies do not contain JSON keys matching /(private_key|private_key_id|client_email)/. Fail builds if present.

keiko: Adding scrubber to ingestion and a unit test in pipeline. PR queued: infra/ingest#341.

sec-bot: automated-update: binding removal initiated (SEC-4231). Forensics bucket: gs://forensic-2812346789/. Next step: legal + partner notification.

linda: Post-ops: rotate svc-ingest key (done), revoke old key (done), redeploy consumer without debug logs (done), ingest scrubber PR opened (infra/ingest#341). Keiko please rotate any CI secrets referencing old key.

satya: CI rotation scheduled; running smoke tests now.

ownen: Forensic question: does the partner have decrypt rights that allowed them to get plaintext earlier? If yes, escalate to SEV and prepare external notification.

mira: For now assume worst-case: partner may have seen plaintext. Legal looped in. Do not request deletion until legal confirms.

sec-bot: automated-update: SEC-4230 containment: true, KMS_binding_removed: true, forensic_snapshot: gs://forensic-2812346789/, next: legal_review.

linda: Follow-up: open postmortem and add an ingest regression test. Also add an RBAC policy gate in infra-as-code to block cross-project decrypts without a documented exception. I'll open a proposal PR.

satya: Good. Scheduling postmortem tomorrow 09:30 PT. Thanks team.

mira: Thanks all. Keep thread updates concise in #sec-4230.
